text:
Anya Pritchard: quick heads up — I opened a docs PR to migrate several SDK snippets to the new function-calling / structured-output patterns and to patch two broken links. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821 :eyes:
Samir Patel: Thanks. Which snippets are the blockers? I saw a failing snippet CI job earlier but didn't dig in.
Anya Pritchard: The Python tool-calling example (tools.invoke) and the compact JSON envelope in the JS guide. Linter output attached in the PR — main complaint is that the example emits free-form text instead of the guarded JSON schema we landed last week.
Miguel Torres: I can take the Python one. Do we want to show the full JSON schema inline or link to the schema defs? My concern is duplication and drift.
Anya Pritchard: Good point. Proposal: show a minimal example inline (fields required: action, args) and add a collapsed block with the full schema link. E.g. inline example:

```python
# minimal tool call example
resp = client.invoke_tool(
    model="redwood-1",
    input="Summarize this",
    tools=[{"name":"summarize","args":{"max_len":120}}]
)
print(resp.json())
```

We should demonstrate the guardrail shape: {"action": "summarize", "args": {...}} and mention fallback parsing tips.
Liz Chen: I'll patch the JS compact envelope example — the current snippet uses an older "invoke" shape. Should we recommend the compact envelope (`{"type":"toolcall","payload":{...}}`) or the explicit action/args?
Samir Patel: Prefer explicit action/args for readability in docs, but include the compact envelope as an advanced section. Also add a note about parser fallbacks: when the model returns plain text, show the regex shim to extract JSON and fall back to the canonical parser.
Miguel Torres: One more CI thing — snippet-run flagged a code fence that had triple-backticks but no language. That causes snippet extraction to fail for the python check. I'll send a tiny patch to add ```python.
Anya Pritchard: Awesome. Action items: Miguel -> PR with python snippet fix + add collapsed full-schema link; Liz -> update JS snippet to explicit action/args and add advanced compact example; Samir -> update the guardrails section wording about parser fallbacks and add short regex shim; I'll update the PR description and mark the broken links to the schema docs fixed.
Liz Chen: quick question: what exact phrasing do we want for the guardrail note re: "always emit valid JSON"? We were avoiding prescriptive language like "must" in public docs.
Anya Pritchard: Use softer guidance: "Prefer emitting the structured JSON shape shown below; include a clear action field and explicit args to make downstream parsing robust." Then show an example and a small subsection titled "If the model outputs non-JSON" with the regex fallback and a short code snippet.
Samir Patel: I'll draft that wording tonight and post a diff in the PR. :shipit:
docs-bot: snippet-ci commented on PR #4821 — python-snippet-check failed (1 of 7). See logs: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/snippet/4821
Miguel Torres: pulled main and pushed python fix — updated fenced block and switched to the canonical action/args example. Leaving a comment in the PR describing the change.
Liz Chen: pushed JS changes, added compact envelope under "Advanced examples", and fixed two links that pointed to the old schema path.
Anya Pritchard: thanks all — I'll re-run the snippet CI once the jobs land. If CI passes, I'll merge and follow up with a small changelog blurb.
Samir Patel: ping me if you want a sanity review before merge.
Anya Pritchard: will do. cc @docs-bot to trigger docs smoke after merge. :white_check_mark:
